Approach and rationale 1.1 Mathematical difficulty and method selection The problem is a finite-dimensional, nonconvex minimax problem on a constrained box/simplex: \[ C_5(h)=\max_{r=0,\ldots,2n-2} dx\; \text{fullcorrelation}_{r}(h,1-h), \qquad dx=2/n,\qquad \sum_i h_i=n/2,\qquad 0\le h_i\le 1. \] Each correlation constraint expands into linear plus negative bilinear products, for example terms of the form \[ h_i(1-h_j)=h_i-h_i h_j, \] so the feasible set \(\{h:C_5(h)\le t\}\) is generally nonconvex. Direct global convex optimization is therefore not applicable, and a CVXPY formulation containing arbitrary bilinear terms cannot be declared a valid convex subproblem. The proposed method therefore uses: - **Uniform constraints and exact evaluation:** every candidate that is reported or selected as a warm start is scored by the supplied official metric \(\max(\text{np.correlate}(h,1-h,\text{full}))*2/n\), not by a relaxed surrogate or manual-only bound. - **A smoothing ladder:** smoothly aggregate near-active lag constraints using exponential or softmax weights. This gives better local descent information than the nondifferentiable maximum when many lags are almost maximal. - **A direct constrained local minimax optimizer:** after smoothing, solve an explicit minimax NLP using SLSQP over all lag inequalities with exact first-order gradient information. - **Multistart, interpolation, and symmetry transforms:** a small set of reachable neighborhood starts and combinatorial-like transforms can move the search to a different basin that a single polish may not reach. - **Conservative fallback:** the parent construction is always treated as a valid feasible benchmark whenever it is internally valid; failure of any local solve, perturbation, projection, or alternative resolution automatically falls back to the best feasible candidate seen so far. The target gap from roughly \(0.38085\) to \(0.3808\) is tiny. To pursue it safely, the procedure combines acceptance only against the **actual evaluator objective**, allowable small absolute and relative tolerances, multi-start intensification, and a suite of basin changes.
